title: The 1975 Pescara piano summit riot
summary: In Pescara, Italy, an unruly crowd disrupts the show and Price answers with Boogie-Woogie.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But the thing that ...always, whenever I was involved in music there (was) always something exciting happening. In 1975 we went to Pescara in Italy...Ray Bryant, Art Hodes/ piano summit. And they had a lot of...a host of musicians. And when we got to Italy, to Pescara, and got into that park, some guy named Cherry. Don Cherry?

He got on the stage and he wouldn't move and the people... the kids wanted to come in free, police was shooting in the crowd, and all of that, so we couldn't perform that night. They asked me where I was going to play. So I told them, "I

came all of this distance to play for money, and I don't know what you mean, that (you know what I mean) I gotta...that I'm not going to play if you can't come in....You know you gotta come in, if you come here to see me, you got to pay, 'cause they got to pay me." So that particular night we didn't play. So they had to postpone the thing 'til the next night.

The next night they had it in a big park. They must have had five hundred soldiers in that place. And they used to what clap (PRICE clapping). So/I...I figured out what I was going to do. I played me a Boogie-Woogie to that rhythm. I played a Boogie-Woogie to that rhythm. They (laughter) didn't understand what happened...I made my little exit and went about my business. That was the last time I saw Charlie Mingus, incidentally. Charlie was half sick, you know.
